lessons.title: Traffic Signs and Signals
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
Texas roads use the same nationally standardized sign shapes and colors as the rest of the country.

- A red octagon always means stop, regardless of the state you are driving in.
- A yellow traffic light warns that the signal is changing to red; stop if you can do so safely.
- Orange diamond-shaped signs mark construction or work zones and often carry reduced speed limits.
- A green arrow allows a protected turn in the direction shown, with no oncoming traffic to yield to.
- Railroad crossing signs and flashing lights require a full stop when a train is approaching.

Recognizing these signs quickly is essential on Texas's mix of rural highways and busy city streets.

lessons.title: Right-of-Way Rules
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
Right-of-way rules apply the same way across Texas's intersections, from rural crossroads to busy city grids.

- At an intersection with no signs or signals, the first vehicle to arrive proceeds first.
- If two vehicles arrive together, the vehicle on the right goes first.
- Pedestrians crossing at a marked or unmarked crosswalk have the right-of-way over vehicles.
- A driver turning left must yield to all oncoming traffic before completing the turn.
- Vehicles already in a roundabout have the right-of-way over vehicles entering it.

Right-of-way rules exist to remove guesswork, but they only work if every driver follows them.

lessons.title: Speed Limits and Safe Following Distance
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
Texas has some of the highest posted speed limits in the country on certain highways, which makes safe following distance even more important.

- The posted speed limit is a maximum for ideal conditions, not a guarantee of safety in all conditions.
- Rural highways may have higher limits, but wildlife, gravel shoulders, and limited lighting can require slower speeds.
- The three-second rule for following distance should be extended to four or more seconds at highway speeds.
- Reduce speed in construction zones even when no workers are visible, since conditions can change quickly.
- Sudden West Texas dust storms can drop visibility to near zero; slow down and, if needed, pull off the road safely.

Matching your speed and following distance to real conditions, not just the posted number, is the core safety skill.

lessons.title: Alcohol, Drugs, and Impaired Driving
lessons.bodyMarkdown:
Impaired driving remains one of the leading causes of serious crashes on Texas roads.

- Any amount of alcohol can measurably slow reaction time and reduce judgment.
- Texas applies a zero-tolerance policy to any detectable alcohol for drivers under 21.
- Certain allergy, pain, and sleep medications carry warnings against operating a vehicle.
- Long, monotonous highway driving increases the risk of drowsy driving, which shares many effects with impairment.
- Planning a sober ride home before drinking removes the decision entirely once impairment sets in.

Separating driving from any form of impairment is the single most effective way to avoid a preventable crash.

questions.prompt: What does a red octagon-shaped sign mean?
questions.explanation: A red octagon is used exclusively for stop signs and always means come to a complete stop.

questions.prompt: What do orange diamond-shaped signs indicate on Texas roads?
questions.explanation: Orange diamond signs mark construction or work zones, which often include reduced speed limits and changed traffic patterns.

questions.prompt: What does a green arrow signal allow?
questions.explanation: A green arrow permits a protected turn in the direction shown, meaning oncoming traffic is stopped and does not need to be yielded to.

questions.prompt: What must a driver do at an active railroad crossing with flashing lights?
questions.explanation: Flashing lights at a railroad crossing require a full stop, since a train may be approaching.

questions.prompt: A solid yellow traffic light means what?
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red; drivers should stop if they can do so safely.

questions.prompt: Why are sign shapes standardized nationally, including in Texas?
questions.explanation: Standardized shapes let drivers recognize a sign's meaning at a glance, even across state lines or in low visibility.

questions.prompt: In a construction zone marked with orange signs, what usually changes?
questions.explanation: Work zones commonly bring reduced speed limits and altered lane patterns to protect workers and drivers.

questions.prompt: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs, who proceeds first?
questions.explanation: The first vehicle to arrive at an uncontrolled intersection has the right-of-way and proceeds first.

questions.prompt: If two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same moment, who yields?
questions.explanation: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right when arrival is simultaneous.

questions.prompt: Do pedestrians have the right-of-way at an unmarked crosswalk?
questions.explanation: Yes, pedestrians generally have the right-of-way at both marked and unmarked crosswalks.

questions.prompt: What must a driver do before completing a left turn?
questions.explanation: A left-turning driver must yield to all oncoming traffic before completing the turn.

questions.prompt: Who has the right-of-way in a roundabout: vehicles already inside or vehicles entering?
questions.explanation: Vehicles already circulating inside a roundabout have the right-of-way over vehicles waiting to enter.

questions.prompt: Why do right-of-way rules only work if every driver follows them?
questions.explanation: Right-of-way rules assign an order, but a driver still has to actually yield for the system to prevent a collision — one driver following the rule is not enough if the other does not.

questions.prompt: At a four-way stop, after stopping, when should a driver proceed?
questions.explanation: After a complete stop, a driver should proceed in the order vehicles arrived, or according to right-of-way rules if arrival was simultaneous.

questions.prompt: Is a high posted speed limit on a rural Texas highway always safe to drive at?
questions.explanation: The posted limit is a maximum for ideal conditions; wildlife, gravel shoulders, or poor lighting can make a lower speed safer.

questions.prompt: At highway speeds, how should the standard three-second following rule be adjusted?
questions.explanation: At higher speeds, stopping distance increases, so the following interval should be extended to four seconds or more.

questions.prompt: Should you slow down in a construction zone even if no workers are visible?
questions.explanation: Yes, because conditions in a work zone can change quickly and workers or equipment may appear without warning.

questions.prompt: What should a driver do if visibility drops sharply during a dust storm?
questions.explanation: Slow down, and if visibility becomes too low to drive safely, pull off the road in a safe location rather than continuing.

questions.prompt: What is the core safety skill described for matching speed to conditions?
questions.explanation: Matching speed and following distance to real, current conditions, not just the posted speed limit, is the core safety skill.

questions.prompt: Why are gravel shoulders on rural highways relevant to speed choice?
questions.explanation: Gravel shoulders reduce traction if a vehicle drifts off the paved surface, so higher speeds leave less margin for safe recovery.

questions.prompt: What following distance mistake is most likely to cause a rear-end crash at highway speed?
questions.explanation: Keeping only the minimum three-second gap at high speed leaves too little time to react if traffic ahead slows suddenly.

questions.prompt: Can a small amount of alcohol affect driving ability?
questions.explanation: Yes, even a small amount of alcohol can measurably slow reaction time and reduce judgment before reaching any legal limit.

questions.prompt: What alcohol policy applies to drivers under 21 in Texas?
questions.explanation: Texas applies a zero-tolerance policy, meaning any detectable alcohol for a driver under 21 is a violation.

questions.prompt: Why might certain allergy or sleep medications be dangerous before driving?
questions.explanation: These medications often carry explicit warnings against operating machinery or vehicles because they can cause drowsiness or slowed reaction time.

questions.prompt: What increases the risk of drowsy driving on long highway trips?
questions.explanation: Long, monotonous stretches of highway driving increase fatigue and the chance of drowsy driving, which shares many effects with impairment.

questions.prompt: What is the benefit of planning a sober ride home before drinking?
questions.explanation: Deciding in advance removes the need to make a judgment call about driving after impairment has already set in.

questions.prompt: What is described as the single most effective way to avoid a preventable crash?
questions.explanation: Separating driving from any form of impairment, whether alcohol, drugs, or extreme fatigue, is the most effective preventive step.

questions.prompt: Why do impaired-driving rules treat drowsiness similarly to alcohol or drug impairment?
questions.explanation: Extreme drowsiness produces effects similar to alcohol or drug impairment, including slowed reaction time and poor judgment, so it carries comparable risk.
